references.text: Abimelech was the son of Gideon's concubine from Shechem, which explains his connection to the city and its inhabitants.
Abimelech persuaded the citizens of Shechem to support him as king, leading to the coronation described in this verse.
Jotham prophesied that fire would come out from Abimelech and consume the citizens of Shechem and the house of Millo, those same people who crowned him.
The house of Millo (the tower of Shechem) was later destroyed by Abimelech, fulfilling Jotham's curse.
Joshua set up a stone under the oak tree at the sanctuary in Shechem, which may be the same place as the oak mentioned in this verse.
Jacob buried the idols under the terebinth tree near Shechem, showing that this place had religious significance.
God revealed himself to Abraham by the terebinth of Moreh at Shechem, establishing the holy character of the site.
Millo is also mentioned in connection with David, who built up Jerusalem, showing that such fortifications were important in Israelite city planning.
